title: A/R Collection: the PDF and CSV match the rows and order on screen
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop works at two locations, and you export A/R Collection for two customers to check it matches the screen.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customers {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} have open documents at both locations on today's date, at least two each, with different amounts.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S3-05 Export One and {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S3-05 Export Two.
  • Starting screen: A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the Customer filter showing {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} ticked and every group expanded (Expand all).
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "Open Balance" header once.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Open the downloaded PDF and compare its rows with the screen, top to bottom.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and compare its rows with the screen.
  6. Without refreshing the page, click the "Date" header.
  7. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu again.
  8. Open the new CSV and compare its rows with the screen.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the rows sort by Open Balance, largest first.
  • Step 2: the PDF downloads as a file and the "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.
  • Step 3: the PDF holds exactly the rows on screen for {Customer-A} and {Customer-B}, in the same order, and has a "Location" column, as the screen does (two locations are in view).
  • Step 4: the CSV downloads and the "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.
  • Step 5: the CSV holds exactly the same rows in the same order, with a "Location" column.
  • Step 6: the rows re-sort by Date.
  • Step 7: the CSV downloads with the "Success" message.
  • Step 8: the new CSV follows the new on-screen order, by Date, not the earlier Open Balance order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S3-R2: “The PDF downloads as a file.”
  • S3-R3: “The PDF and the CSV contain exactly the rows on screen for the chosen as-of date, customer or vendor and locations, in the on-screen sort, including a sort changed after an earlier export, without refreshing the page.”
  • S3-R6: “The Location column appears in the export under the same rule as on screen (Story 6).”
  • S3-R10: “A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Export succeeds | "Success", "Data exported successfully." | Success toast, as on the other reports”
  • S6-R2: “The column is shown when two or more locations are ticked (All locations counts when the report's list has two or more) and hidden when one or none is ticked.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 2 "Export" (board Export.dc.html); page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p2-export-menu-pdf-and-csv.png: figure "Export menu: PDF and CSV" (This build (after)), board "2. Export"
  • ar-ap-p4-opens-on-all-locations.png: figure "Opens on All locations" (This build (after)), board "4. Location filter and Location column"

The design's own words:

  • "The native ⋯ Export menu on all six reports. Files hold exactly the rows on screen, in screen order, with the as-of date and locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor when chosen. S3-R1 to S3-R8, S3-R8a." (caption of "Export menu: PDF and CSV")
  • "Native filter row: As of, Customer, Past due, then Location, which opens on "Location: All locations". Untouched, the report matches today. Column labelled "Location", after Date. S5-R1, S5-R2, S5-R5, S6-R1 to S6-R3." (caption of "Opens on All locations")
